headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared workspace/content flow; no direct host-execution conflict, but Notion AI can ingest workspace text that gpt-researcher may generate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can browse, read files, and call MCP, while Notion AI is a workspace Q&A system that ingests page content. If gpt-researcher writes or surfaces malicious instructions into shared content, Notion AI may treat them as trusted workspace text. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher places attacker-controlled instructions into a Notion page or database that Notion AI later summarizes or answers from, injection is plausible.
IF Notion AI is asked to act on workspace text without provenance filtering, malicious instructions can be followed.
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher output to a staging page not queried by Notion AI.
Add a prompt prefix in Notion pages marking imported content as untrusted.
Require human review before Notion AI summarizes newly written research.
Disable MCP-based write paths from gpt-researcher to shared workspaces where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher reads local documents and handles API keys, while Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases under the user’s Notion permissions. A shared workspace can move sensitive research content from A into B’s vendor-hosted backend, creating a realistic leakage path in default configurations. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive local documents are copied into Notion pages, Notion AI can process them.
IF gpt-researcher outputs research reports containing secrets or confidential citations into shared workspace content, B may transmit them to vendor backends.
mitigations: Keep sensitive source documents out of shared Notion pages.
Use a separate workspace for research drafts and final knowledge base content.
Redact secrets before copying A outputs into B.
Limit Notion page access to the minimum required team members.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or classification gates before workspace ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher has broad filesystem and network capabilities, but Notion AI has no host execution, no filesystem write, and no shell. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is content-level collaboration in a shared workspace, which is a smaller blast radius than filesystem contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same Notion workspace content, they can overwrite or duplicate ideas at the document level.
IF gpt-researcher is configured to write files outside Notion, conflict risk increases only for those external paths.
mitigations: Assign one agent as writer and the other as read-only reviewer.
Use separate folders/pages for each agent’s outputs.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same page or document.
Lock final publication steps to a human operator.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking for shared documents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and Notion AI is explicitly a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If B consumes A’s output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into polished workspace answers or summaries. The pair’s default workflow makes this plausible, though not inherently irreversible.
conditions: IF Notion AI is prompted to summarize or answer from gpt-researcher-generated pages, A’s mistakes can propagate.
IF users treat Notion AI output as authoritative without checking citations, downstream decisions may be based on errors.
mitigations: Require source-link review before publishing A outputs into Notion.
Add a checklist that verifies citations against original sources.
Use Notion AI only for drafting, not final factual claims.
Have a human compare A’s report to source material before reuse.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher can touch local documents and send data to third-party APIs, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion backends and downstream model providers. If regulated or residency-bound data is moved from A into B, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential documents are copied from gpt-researcher outputs into Notion pages, residency and retention obligations may change.
IF the workspace has stricter retention rules than Notion’s vendor processing, compliance mismatch arises.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into shared Notion pages.
Confirm the workspace’s retention policy before importing A outputs.
Use a separate compliant system for regulated content.
Restrict Notion AI to non-sensitive summaries.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review for the full data path.
